name: Laban
description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: Jacob was sent to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah. Rebekah herself was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother; the family line was kept in place, generation after generation going back to their own kindred.

note.label: Genesis 28: The Charge and the Vow at Bethel

points: Jacob asks, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor, and the men of Haran know him. Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran, so Laban dwells in that area because the family remained there when Terah stopped at Haran.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

points: Laban said unto Jacob, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh. In the scriptures that phrase means we are family; Jacob abode with him a month, and Laban, because Jacob was his brother, asked what his wages should be.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

points: Laban asked Jacob to tarry: I have learned by experience that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake. Laban understood that with Jacob in his household he was increasing, and he offered to appoint Jacob his wages.

note.label: Genesis 30: Trouble in the Flesh and a Righteous Hire

points: So Jacob was Laban's shepherd. He took care of the sheep, the cattle. He was a shepherd just like Abel was a shepherd, and Esau was the man of the field just like Cain was a man of the field. You see where I'm going with this?

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Jacob heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that was our father's, and of that which was our father's hath he gotten all this glory; and Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and behold, it was not toward him as before.

Remember, Laban had just acknowledged, I have learned by experience that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake; now he is looking at Jacob sideways because of what his sons said. That is exactly why Jacob said, So shall my righteousness answer for me: he dealt righteously in the open so his dealings would be his answer.

note.label: Genesis 31: The Return Home and Laban's Idols

points: Laban went to shear his sheep, and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's. Remember what we read in Proverbs about beauty: yes, she was fine, but she was a thief. She might have been a fine thief, but she was a thief.

note.label: Genesis 31: The Return Home and Laban's Idols

cases.name: Laban and the changed wages
cases.charge: Changing his hired servant’s wages ten times, and giving the elder daughter in place of the younger
cases.preview: Laban of the house of Nahor, an idolater as his fathers were, received Jacob as his own bone and flesh, then took seven years of work for Rachel and delivered Leah, charged seven more, and changed…
